question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2y}{12}, & \,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}+2y}{12}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}+\frac{y}{6})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{36}+\frac{xy}{6}]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =\frac{27}{36}+\frac{3y}{6}-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{y}{2} \\  & =\frac{2y+3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y+3}{4}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{x}^{2}+2y}{12})}{(\frac{2y+3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+2y}{3(2y+3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2y}{3(2y+3)}, & \,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
